LESSON: SINGING GAMES- AFRICAN STYLE

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Performing and Display
Topic 2.1: Singing Games- African Style
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Singing Games- African Style, part of Performing and Display in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: Why are singing games performed?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Singing Games- African Style together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: The learner confidently makes a variety of body movements which are appropriate while performing the African singing

games.

• Learning to learn: The learner performs African singing games while making different pattern formations learnt in earlier grades,

• Citizenship: The learner takes pride in performing African singing games from diverse Kenyan communities.

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner takes different roles while performing an African style singing game.

• Unity: The learner works with others as they perform African style singing games.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Personal hygiene: The learner collects locally available materials for making simple paper costumes.

African style.

Link to other learning areas:

Indigenous Language Activities: The learners sing varied indigenous songs in the African singing games.

Suggested learning resources:

Open safe quiet space, digital devices: laptops, tablets, smart phones, computers, Sound instruments , whiskers clothes and flags, assorted

props for singing or dancing games, song book, Audio/visual recordings, relevant attire, landing mats
